sanskrit:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥
transliteration:
karmaṇy-evādhikāras te mā phaleṣhu kadāchana
mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stvakarmaṇi
translation: You have a right to perform your prescribed duties, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions. Never consider yourself the sole cause of the results, nor let your mind be attached to inaction.
simpleExplanation: When we focus entirely on the outcome (such as exam grades, approval, or whether we succeed or fail), our anxiety skyrockets. This verse advises shifting 100% of our energy to the effort right in front of us, letting go of the obsession with things we cannot control.
whyThisVerse: This verse directly addresses anxiety regarding the future and performance stress by distinguishing between what is within your control (your immediate action) and what is not (the exact future outcome).

transliteration:
mātrā-sparśhās tu kaunteya śhītoṣhṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ
āgamāpāyino ’nityās tans-titikṣhasva bhārata
translation: The contact of the senses with their objects gives rise to feelings of cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These experiences are fleeting and impermanent; learn to endure them patiently.
simpleExplanation: Hard moments and painful feelings arrive like seasons—just as winter gives way to spring. When experiencing emotional discomfort, remembering that this feeling is impermanent helps us remain balanced and patient.
whyThisVerse: This verse was selected because you are experiencing a difficult emotional wave. It reminds us that emotions arise, peak, and dissolve naturally.

sanskrit:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते।
सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते॥
transliteration:
dhyāyato viṣhayān puṁsaḥ saṅgas teṣhūpajāyate
saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho ’bhijāyate
translation: When a person constantly broods on objects of the senses, attachment to them develops. From attachment arises longing, and from thwarted longing arises anger.
simpleExplanation: Frustration and irritation often start small: we fixate on how we think things 'should' be. When reality clashes with our expectation, that attachment transforms into anger.
whyThisVerse: This verse clarifies the psychological root of frustration: it shows how over-focusing on an unmet expectation triggers irritation and mental agitation.

sanskrit:
क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति॥
transliteration:
krodhād bhavati sammohaḥ sammohāt smṛiti-vibhramaḥ
smṛiti-bhranśhād buddhi-nāśho buddhi-nāśhāt praṇaśhyati
translation: From anger arises delusion; from delusion comes confusion of memory; from confusion of memory comes loss of reason; and from loss of reason, a person falls into ruin.
simpleExplanation: When we get deeply angry or overwhelmed, our rational judgment clouds over. We forget what matters most and say or do things we regret. Pausing and calming down restores our ability to think clearly.
whyThisVerse: This verse highlights the importance of stepping back before reacting when experiencing heightened anger or frustration.

sanskrit:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमप्नोति न कामकामी॥
transliteration:
āpūryamāṇam achala-pratiṣhṭhaṁ samudram āpaḥ praviśhanti yadvat
tadvat kāmā yaṁ praviśhanti sarve sa śhāntim āpnoti na kāma-kāmī
translation: Just as the ocean remains undisturbed while rivers continuously flow into it, so the person into whom all desires enter without causing disturbance attains peace, not the one who strives to satisfy every desire.
simpleExplanation: External events and chaotic thoughts will always come at us like rushing rivers. True peace does not come from stopping the world; it comes from having a mind as vast and deep as the ocean, remaining still underneath the surface waves.
whyThisVerse: This verse provides a grounding image of steady stillness and resilience amidst external chaos.

sanskrit:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्।
स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः॥
transliteration:
śhreyān swa-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣhṭhitāt
swa-dharme nidhanaṁ śhreyaḥ para-dharmo bhayāvahaḥ
translation: It is far better to perform one's own natural duty, even if imperfectly, than to master the duty of another. Following another's path brings fear and disharmony.
simpleExplanation: Comparing your life, career, or progress to other people always creates anxiety and self-doubt. You have your own unique nature and pace. Walking your own path sincerely is always better than living someone else's life.
whyThisVerse: This verse speaks directly to self-comparison, imposter syndrome, and doubt about your own journey.

sanskrit:
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः॥
transliteration:
uddhared ātmanātmānaṁ nātmānam avasādayet
ātmaiva hyātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ
translation: Elevate yourself through the power of your own mind, and do not degrade yourself. For the mind can be your greatest friend, or your greatest enemy.
simpleExplanation: Our own internal self-talk can either lift us up or tear us down. When you treat yourself with gentle discipline and kindness, your mind becomes your closest ally in overcoming difficult circumstances.
whyThisVerse: This verse reminds us of personal agency and encourages positive, compassionate internal dialogue when feeling discouraged.

sanskrit:
बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः।
अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत्॥
transliteration:
bandhur ātmātmanas tasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ
anātmanas tu śhatrutve vartetātmaiva śhatru-vat
translation: For one who has mastered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. But for one who has not, the mind acts as an enemy from within.
simpleExplanation: An untrained mind jumps from worry to worry, generating imaginary problems. By practicing simple mindfulness and gentle awareness, we train our thoughts to support us rather than oppose us.
whyThisVerse: This verse was selected to guide overthinking into gentle mental mastery and self-awareness.

sanskrit:
नात्यश्नतस्तु योगोऽस्ति न चैकान्तमनश्नतः।
न चाति स्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन॥
transliteration:
nāty-aśhnatas tu yogo ’sti na chaikāntam anaśhnataḥ
na chāti-svapna-śhīlasya jāgrato naiva chārjuna
translation: Meditation and balance cannot be attained by one who eats too much or starves, nor by one who sleeps too much or stays awake all night.
simpleExplanation: Exhaustion and stress often stem from physical extremes—such as skipping sleep or working without breaks. Finding harmony in basic daily rhythms (sleep, food, rest) is the foundation of mental peace.
whyThisVerse: This verse points out that peace of mind requires caring for bodily rhythms and avoiding burnout.

sanskrit:
असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम्।
अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते॥
transliteration:
asanśhayaṁ mahā-bāho mano durnigrahaṁ chalam
abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa cha gṛihyate
translation: Undoubtedly, the mind is restless and very difficult to curb. But it can be mastered through regular practice (abhyasa) and the cultivation of non-attachment (vairagya).
simpleExplanation: Krishna validates Arjuna's honest confession: yes, the mind is restless, and everyone struggles with it. You don't master it overnight; you gently bring it back through daily practice and letting go of perfectionism.
whyThisVerse: This verse reassures that mental restlessness is completely normal and gives a constructive solution: steady, gentle practice over time.

sanskrit:
अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च।
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी॥
transliteration:
adveṣhṭā sarva-bhūtānāṁ maitraḥ karuṇa eva cha
nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ kṣhamī
translation: One who is free from malice toward all beings, friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and egoism, balanced in joy and sorrow, and forgiving.
simpleExplanation: Holding resentment drains our own energy. When we treat others and ourselves with compassion, forgiveness, and less ego, our heart becomes light and free.
whyThisVerse: This verse was selected to offer perspective on interpersonal tension, encouraging forgiveness and empathy.

sanskrit:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज।
अहं त्वां सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः॥
transliteration:
sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṁ śharaṇaṁ vraja
ahaṁ tvāṁ sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣhayiṣhyāmi mā śhuchaḥ
translation: Abandon all varieties of anxiety and surrender unto the Supreme Truth. I shall liberate you from all fears and burdens. Do not grieve.
simpleExplanation: When we have tried everything and still feel heavy, carrying the weight of the entire world on our shoulders is unnecessary. Trust in the greater reality, let go of the burden, and know that you are supported.
whyThisVerse: This verse provides ultimate solace and assurance when feeling utterly overwhelmed by life's burdens.
